title: There were so many times during this show where I just thought “WHY i...
transcript: I think it's time to talk about Back to the Future the Musical and the way that we update classic stories. Because Back to the Future doesn't really update anything from its source material, it's almost a direct one to one comparison with the movie. And as a result, a lot of it felt really dated to me. Like for example, in the movie there is a scene where Marty’s father (in high school) is watching his future wife through her bedroom window from a tree outside her house, and it's creepy… And in the show, they for some reason choose to musicalize this, so he now sings an entire song from the tree about watching this woman through her bedroom window and it just feels really creepy especially in 2023. Another example is Marty’s brother, who at the beginning of the show is working at McDonalds, which the show frames as like: “He has no future!” “He lacks ambition!” “Working at fast food is bad!” and then at the end of the show when Marty you know “fixes” the present he works for generic business and that's “good” “He turned his life around!” and it just feels really like reductive to be like “Working at fast food bad, working for business good!” And these are all very small aspects of the story that feel easily fixable. Like there are other ways to show that a guy is longing for a girl from afar but doesn't have the confidence to go up to her. And there are other ways to show that a character lacks career ambition that isn't just “oh, let's just put them in a McDonald's.” And I wish that the writers and the producers thought a little bit more critically about the messages in their show, both big and small, and how they would be received by 2023 audiences. And rather than focusing on “Let's just make the movie on stage, because people like the movie and therefore they will like the show if it's exactly like the movie” they took a step back and said “Okay, what elements of the movie maybe haven't aged the best? and what should we update for modern audiences and modern sensibilities?” And I just don't think that they did that.
reasoning: The reviewer criticizes the musical for being a dated, direct adaptation that fails to update problematic elements from the source material. They specifically call out creepy and reductive content that feels inappropriate for modern audiences, indicating they would not recommend the show.
keyQuote: And I just don't think that they did that.
